newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK FRNS FIRM ON CBANK BUYING, FORWARDS BIASED UP.
newsitem.headline: GREEK FRNS FIRM ON CBANK BUYING, FORWARDS BIASED UP.

text.p: Greek fixed coupon bonds were stable at slightly lower levels in late dealings but FRNs gained after the central bank bought floaters due 2004 in intraday trade to prop up prices before the June 26 FRN auction, dealers said.
Forex forwards were exhibiting an upward bias in late trade, short-run depos were slightly lower but long-run depos were up and ecu/drachma was trapped in the tight 309.08/18 range.
"Long-dated depos are steady at higher levels but short-run depos have eased a bit," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "The forward curve is also up on funding for the seven-year floaters."
Greece will auction 150 billion drachmas of seven-year FRNs on June 26. The first coupon is equal to 10.40 percent and gross selling commision stands at 1.10 percent.

Fixed coupon bonds rebounded after suffering earlier losses to stabilise at marginally lower levels in late trade but FRNs were firmer after the central bank bought seven-year floaters due 2004, dealers said.

"Fixed coupon bonds have gained back some ground and trade at slightly lower levels in late dealings," said a dealer. "Seven-year FRNs due 2004 have firmed on some central bank buying in the secondary market."
Dealers estimated the amount of FRNs bought by the central bank around 1.0 billion drachmas.
"The central bank tried to shore up FRN prices before the auction by buying FRNs and pumping money into the system to ease interbank rates," said a bond trader at a foreign bank.
The discount margin on FRNs due 2004 has eased to 95 basis points from 98 basis points earlier.
"The discount margin even hit 100 basis points before falling back on the central bank intervention," the dealer said.

The gross redemption yield of the benchmark 10-year coupon bond was up at 9.12 percent, the five-year bond due 2002 was yielding 9.75 percent from 9.74 percent around mid-session and the three-year bond yield due 2000 was 10.18 percent.
The mark was quoted at 157.69/74 from Tuesday's 157.715 fix, the dollar at 271.81/91 drachmas from 271.900 and the ecu at 309.08/18 from 309.140 drachmas.
"Ecu/drachma is easier trading around 309.10 in late quiet dealing," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank.
